review_findings: The proposed compiler is upstream of and terminates at the current WorkflowSpec parser, so it does not create a peer runtime or graph authority.
The CLI makes generated declarations maintainable without a Host while leaving ChatGPT and Codex available as optional natural-language composers.
Strict schemas, safe loading, bounded write scope, and explicit mutating capabilities close the main authoring trust-boundary risks.
TaskRun VALIDATING semantics remain explicit in the source declaration and compiled plan; Graph END cannot claim completion.
The path set is limited to control-plane authoring, its root route, tests, schemas, and architecture documentation.

skill_rule_mappings.assessment: authoring compiles into workflow_registry.parse_workflow_spec and workflow_graph_contract rather than interpreting a parallel graph
the declaration contract requires transition_to VALIDATING and authority TaskRun

skill_rule_mappings.rule: Observation and capability binding are not write authority
skill_rule_mappings.assessment: mutating Skill contracts require explicit workspace.write while existing runtime guards remain unchanged
